reason: The passage (1 Samuel 28-30) depicts Hebrew leaders (Saul and Samuel) in crisis and delivering dire prophecies, but does not show them acting with antagonism toward the Hebrew people. Saul is portrayed as fearful and weak in leadership, consulting a medium despite having banned such practices, but he is not shown actively opposing or acting hostilely toward his people. Samuel delivers a grim prophecy of defeat, but this is presented as divine judgment, not antagonistic action. The only explicit antagonism shown in the text runs in the opposite direction: the Hebrew people wanting to stone David (a Hebrew leader) when they discover Ziklag has been raided. The passage illustrates failed leadership and tragic consequences, but not deliberate hostility from leaders toward their people.
